capabilities: Browse JSON, JSONL, and NDJSON files as a tree
Filter nodes by key, value, or JSON Pointer path
Navigate large structures via an outline panel
Copy raw JSON or individual JSON Pointer paths
Show syntax-highlighted source with line numbers
disambiguation: Not a JSON editor or formatter; it only displays data read-only and never writes back to files.
extras: Read-only by design: never writes to disk, so it cannot reformat or corrupt data files. Makes no network requests; writes to the clipboard only on explicit copy-button clicks. JSONL rendering is capped at the first 1,000 valid records, with additional valid records counted and invalid ones reported as per-line parse errors. Beta testing via BRAT is mentioned.
problem: Obsidian shows JSON and JSONL files as raw unformatted text, making large configuration files, logs, and exports hard to inspect.
summary: Read-only viewer that opens .json, .jsonl, and .ndjson files as a filterable tree with outline navigation and syntax-highlighted source.
